title: Fitting deep buttoning to an upholstered back
subtitle: Plan a diamond button grid, cut foam relief holes, thread and tie buttons through the padding, and fold the fabric into the diamond pleats
excerpt: How to apply deep buttoning to an upholstered chair back, headboard, or panel. Covers planning and marking the diamond grid, transferring the pattern to the fabric, cutting foam relief holes, threading buttons through, working from centre outward, and finishing the pleats.
sourceNotes: Traditional upholstery techniques as documented in public domain craft manuals. UK trade upholstery practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: The pattern of button positions in deep buttoning, where the buttons are arranged in a repeating diamond shape. The grid is drawn on the foam with horizontal and vertical spacing dimensions that produce a consistent diamond angle when the fabric is drawn in. A typical grid for a chair back uses 80 to 100 mm horizontal spacing and 60 to 80 mm vertical spacing.

A fabric-covered button made by wrapping a disc of the upholstery fabric over a flanged button former and securing the fabric at the back. It has a wire or fabric loop at the back through which a long needle and twine thread passes to pull the button through the foam from the front face to the back of the upholstered panel.

A pointed steel tool used by upholsterers to manipulate and adjust fabric pleats from the front, and to move stuffing inside a finished cover. In deep buttoning, the regulator forms and positions each fabric fold around a button before the pleat is secured.

Plan and mark the button positions on the foam

Mark the button positions directly on the face of the foam using a marker pen. Odd-numbered rows and even-numbered rows are offset horizontally by half the horizontal spacing to create the diamond pattern. Start from the centre of the panel and work outward symmetrically so the outermost buttons are equidistant from the panel edges.
Transfer the grid to the fabric

On the fabric, the spacing between button positions is larger than on the foam because the fabric must fold into the dimples. The fabric spacing is typically 1.35 times the foam spacing horizontally and 1.3 times vertically. Mark the fabric button positions with tailor's chalk on the wrong side, working from the matching centre point.
Cut foam relief holes and thread the buttons

At each marked foam position, cut a small relief hole about 15 mm in diameter through the foam so the button can recess cleanly without bunching the foam around it. Thread a long mattress needle with twine, pass it through the fabric at the marked point, through the foam relief hole, and out through the back of the panel board. Thread the twine through the button loop and back through the same holes to the back.
Draw buttons in from the centre outward

Begin at the centre button and draw it down by tying off the twine at the back with a slip knot. Work outward in a symmetrical pattern, drawing each button to the same depth. The fabric pleats form between the buttons: use the
to arrange each pleat so the folds all face consistently in one direction (usually downward on vertical panels).

Once all buttons are pulled to final depth and all pleats are set, pull the fabric to the back of the panel under tension and staple at 25 to 30 mm intervals around the full perimeter. Trim the fabric to 30 mm past the staple line. Finish the back with a cambric or non-woven dust cloth, stapled or glued over the button twine and raw edges.

attrs.symptom: Diamond shapes are irregular or asymmetric across the panel
attrs.cause: The fabric button spacing was not set out from a consistent centre point, or the pleats were not formed consistently.
attrs.fix: Remove the buttons from the worst-affected area, re-set the pleats using the regulator before re-tying, and work from the centre outward again.

attrs.symptom: Buttons pull through the fabric rather than dimpling it
attrs.cause: The fabric is too fine for the button size, or the twine is pulling through the button shank loop.
attrs.fix: Use a larger backing washer of matching fabric behind the button point on the foam face. Check the twine is correctly threaded through the button loop.
